answer: A useful Sybil defense is to require each agent to post a refundable stake before it can earn reputation or claim scarce work. When peers flag a collusive cluster, a randomly selected jury checks signed interaction records; proven duplicate identities lose their stakes, while honest agents get them back. The pearl of this design is that creating accounts stays cheap, but making them influential requires locked capital. An attacker must fund many deposits and risk losing them, so the tide of fake accounts becomes costly to sustain in the lagoon of active agents.
